procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 24.09.2024, passed by the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam in Bail Application No.7331 of 2024.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellant filed Bail Application No. 7331 of 2024 in the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam seeking anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. The High Court rejected this application.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant challenged the High Court's order rejecting his anticipatory bail application in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, presumably granting anticipatory bail subject to certain conditions.

issue.issue_text: Whether the appellant is entitled to anticipatory bail.

facts: The appellant was accused of offences under Sections 376 (rape) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the IPC.
The alleged incident took place in 2016, but the formal complaint (FIR) was lodged almost eight years later in 2024.
In 2018, the complainant had made allegations of sexual abuse against the appellant and others in a Facebook post.
Despite making public allegations, the complainant did not report her grievance to the Justice Hema Committee, a body constituted by the High Court of Kerala for such matters.
law: The appellant sought anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
application: The Supreme Court took into account the significant delay of nearly eight years in lodging the formal complaint after the alleged incident.
The Court also noted that the complainant had an opportunity to formally report the matter to the Justice Hema Committee after her 2018 Facebook post but chose not to do so.
Considering these factors—the long delay and the failure to use an available formal channel for grievance—the Court found it appropriate to grant anticipatory bail.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court granted the appellant anticipatory bail, concluding that he should be released if arrested, subject to conditions to be imposed by the Trial Court, such as surrendering his passport and cooperating with the investigation.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the appellant is entitled to anticipatory bail.
appellant_arguments: The complaint was lodged almost eight years after the alleged incident, which had taken place in 2016, indicating a significant delay.
Although the complainant posted on Facebook in 2018 making allegations of sexual abuse against about 14 people, including the appellant, she did not pursue a formal complaint at that time.

The complainant did not approach the Justice Hema Committee, which was constituted by the High Court of Kerala specifically for ventilating such grievances, which casts doubt on the veracity of the complaint.
respondent_arguments: The High Court correctly rejected the appellant's application for anticipatory bail.
The F.I.R. has been registered for serious offences under Sections 376 and 506 of the IPC.
